description:
Read the queryable field catalogue AND the filter-AST grammar for this account's own lead corpus. CALL THIS FIRST — before authoring any filter.

WHAT YOU GET BACK, and why one call is enough:
- fields[]: every askable field, each with its own key, type, label, allowed operators, and (for enumerable fields) a values_endpoint. The KEY is a catalogue lookup, NOT a column name — an unlisted key is refused, so there is nothing to be clever about.
- ast: the grammar. operators_by_type (which operators a field's TYPE allows), valueless_operators (is_empty / is_not_empty take NO value — sending one is a 422, not an ignored extra), list_operators (their value is an array), operator_aliases (">=" and "gte" both work), value_rules, limits, error_codes, and a worked example.
- limits: 20 conditions, depth 3, 5 groups, 100 values per list. A valid filter can still be refused for being too big.
- presets: ready-made filters for the four questions people actually ask — never crawled, no email found, email found but never verified, never pinned to VayaPin. PREFER A PRESET when it matches the user's intent; it is server-authored, so it cannot disagree with the validator.

DO NOT author a filter from memory or from a field name that "looks right". The catalogue is the vocabulary and it is the whole vocabulary. Static per deployment — read it once per session and reuse it.
